The Diffusion Controller looks for the initial condition that grows into a chosen Gray-Scott pattern.
It follows DiffusionPDE [@huang2024diffusionpde]: a U-Net denoiser [@karras2022elucidating] learns what consistent pairs of early and late states look like, and a search starting from pure noise is steered towards the target late state while the denoiser keeps the pair physically plausible.
The result is judged by the re-simulation error: the distance between the target and the state obtained by running the solver forward from the recovered start.
Results and pictures are on [Pattern Forcing](../gray-scott-inversion/index.qmd); this page records how the model was built and where it fails.

## How the data were simulated

The Gray-Scott model has an activator u and a substrate v.
Training scenes were simulated on a square with no-flux boundaries, on grids of 16, 32 and 64 cells, with a spacing of 2 length units.
Diffusion is solved exactly in a cosine basis and the reaction by an explicit step, with time step 1.218.

Each scene starts from a random field: u is half of the positive part of a Gaussian random field, and v is 1 everywhere.
The full state (u, v) is stored at steps 50 and 100; step 0 is never shown to the model.
A scene is kept only if it is finite and still patterned at the end.

{{< include charts/data.html >}}

## Why these parameters

- **Feed a = 0.02842, kill b = 0.05368.** Kept from the earlier project this one grew from; the point lies just above the fold below which no pattern survives (a > 4(a+b)², ratio 1.054).
- **Diffusivities 0.3 for u, 1.0 for v.** The activator must diffuse more slowly than the substrate.
- **Grid spacing 2.** A spacing of 4 pinned strokes to the grid axes; 2 matches a much finer reference within about 10%.
- **Time step 1.218.** Set for accuracy, dt·(a+b) ≤ 0.1; the diffusion step is stable at any size.

A later screen of the (a, b) plane confirmed how narrow the patterned region is: patterns survive only for a in 0.030–0.057 and b in 0.054–0.062.

## Which U-Nets

The default denoiser is the DDPM++ U-Net with EDM noise conditioning, 1.7 million parameters.
Three other U-Net designs were trained at matched size on the 16 × 16 data and scored on the same 20 held-out scenes.

{{< include charts/unets.html >}}

The differences between designs are smaller than the differences between scenes (interquartile range ±0.03–0.06), so the choice of U-Net matters little.
U²-Net beat the default on the long-horizon task below and became the reference there.

## Where it fails: starts of settled patterns

The method works while the pattern is still forming.
Asked to go from a settled pattern back to its start, it fails, and more data does not help.

{{< include charts/windows.html >}}

The reason is that settled patterns forget where they came from.
A single blob reaches its steady state by about step 300–400, and from then on the state stops changing.
On the step 50 → 300 task, the different starts that all reproduce the data are as far from each other (0.251) as from the true start (0.263).
Taking the best of 8 draws and polishing it fixes the future, a re-simulation error of 0.009, but not the past: the recovered start stays wrong.

## Physics search: simpler starts without learning

Physics search drops the network.
It writes the start as a few primitives, a blob (centre, width, strength: 4 numbers) or a line (two ends, width, strength: 6 numbers), and fits them by gradient descent through the solver [@kingma2015adam; @ledimet1986variational].
Primitives are added one at a time where the misfit is largest [@mallat1993matching; @denoyelle2020sliding].
Simplicity is counted as the fewest numbers needed to redraw a start.

On 20 held-out 16 × 16 scenes the true starts need a median of 24 numbers.

{{< include charts/physics.html >}}

Physics search therefore trades accuracy for starts that are two to three times simpler than the true ones.
It was tested only on scenes made by the simulator with uniform coefficients, and it scales badly: the blob-and-line search reaches 0.220 on 32 × 32 and 0.520 on 64 × 64, against 0.015 and 0.066 for the Diffusion Controller.
